7798.t: BM6542: Enzyme Technology and Industrial Applications
7798.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6542 : Enzyme Technology and Industrial Applications { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Introduction to Enzymes (10 Contact Hours)
Enzymes, general characters, biological vs chemical catalysis, nomenclature, Structure and function of enzymes, Structural classification, enzyme denaturation - renaturation Specificity, Enzyme structural components, Enzyme activity, Turnover number, Specific Activity. RNA Enzymes. Enzyme catalysis, Initial velocity studies, Estimation of Michaelis Menten parameters, Effect of pH and temperature on enzyme activity, kinetics of inhibition.
Module 2: Enzyme Immobilization (6 Contact Hours)
Techniques of enzyme immobilization kinetics of immobilized enzymes, effect of solute, partition & diffusion on the kinetics of immobilized enzymes, design and configuration of immobilized enzyme reactors applications and economics of immobilized enzyme technology.
Module 3: Production of Enzymes (7 Contact Hours)
Raw material, pretreatment methods, choice of microorganisms, fermentation methods: solid state fermentation, submerged fermentation, Other production methods. Cloning, Expression in Host and Extraction Strategies.
Module 4: Purification of Enzymes (8 Contact Hours)
Introduction, traditional enzyme purification methods, Ion exchange chromatography, Gel filtration, Bio-affinity Chromatography, Hydrophobic interaction chromatography, Hydroxyapatite Chromatography, Enzyme purification protocol. Purification of Recombinant Enzymes: Immobilized Metal Affinity Chromatography, Affinity chromatography with protein tags
Module 5: Use cases for Industrial Applications (6 Contact Hours)
Production and purification of large-scale enzyme in the area of: medicine, food, environment, and lifestyle.

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce the catalytic mechanisms of enzyme reactions, with an emphasis on: cofactors in enzymology, mechanisms of group transfer reactions and oxido-reduction reactions
2 .

To realise the various applications of enzymes in the fields of food industry, pharmaceutical industry and other applications

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Students will be able to learn about enzyme structure, function and enzyme catalyzed reactions
2. Students will be able to understand engineering principles for enzyme production at large scale.
3. Students will be able to design a production and purification strategy for a hypothetical enzyme of choice.

Essential Reading

1 .

Najafpour, G.D.,, Biochemical Engineering and Biotechnology, Elsevier Publishers , 2015

2 .

Katoh, S., J. Horiuchi and F. Yoshida,, Biochemical Engineering: A Textbook for Engineers, Chemists and Biologists, Wiley publications , 2016

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Wolfgang, A.,, Enzymes in Industry: Production and Applications, Wiley publications , 2007

2 .

NIIR Board of Consultants & Engineers, Enzymes Biotechnology Handbook, Asia Pacific Business Press, India , 2004

8822.t: CE3711: Computer Application in Civil Engineering
8822.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE3711 : Computer Application in Civil Engineering { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to Computer Applications in Civil Engineering [3 Hours]
Importance of software tools in civil engineering
Overview of commonly used software: MATLAB, ABAQUS, RS 2, REVIT and other civil engineering software
Basics of computational modelling and simulation

Module 2 :

Programming and Computational Tools in Civil Engineering [3 Hours]
Basics of MATLAB/ PYTHON for civil engineering applications
Automation of calculations (structural analysis, traffic flow, material properties)
Data analysis and visualization for civil engineering problems

Module 3 :

Finite Element Modelling and Analysis [6 Hours]
Basics of the Finite Element Method (FEM)
Introduction to ABAQUS/ANSYS for structural analysis
Static, dynamic, and buckling analysis of structures
Case study on FEM applications in civil engineering

Module 4 :

Geotechnical Engineering Applications [6 Hours]
Slope stability analysis and foundation design (RocScience 2/Slide 2)

Module 5 :

Pavement Engineering Applications [3 Hours]
Pavement analysis and design using software (RocScience 2/Slide 2)

Module 6 :

Hydrology and Water Resources Engineering Software [3 Hours]
Introduction to HEC-RAS/ HEC-HMS
Simulation of precipitation-runoff process/ flood events

Module 7 :

Building Information Modelling (BIM) in Civil Engineering [3 Hours]
Overview of BIM and its advantages
Introduction to Revit for architectural and structural modelling
Clash detection and coordination using Navisworks
BIM-based project management and collaboration

Module 8 :

Construction Management and Planning Software [3 Hours]
Introduction to Primavera P6/ Microsoft Project
Scheduling, resource allocation, and cost estimation
Risk analysis and project monitoring techniques
Case study on project scheduling

Course Objective

1 .

Understand the Role of Computer Applications in Civil Engineering – Explore the importance of software tools for drafting, analysis, design, and project management in civil engineering.
2 .

Develop Proficiency in Structural and Geotechnical Analysis Software – Gain hands-on experience with any suitable software such as ABAQUS, and Rocscience for structural, transportation and geotechnical modelling
3 .

Apply Hydrological, BIM, and Project Management Tools – Utilize HEC-RAS/HEC-HMS, Revit, and Primavera P6 for water resource management, building information modelling, and construction planning.
4 .

Integrate Computational and Programming Tools for Civil Engineering Solutions – Use MATLAB for automating calculations, data analysis, and simulation of civil engineering problems.

Course Outcome

1 .

Master Civil Engineering Software Tools – Demonstrate proficiency in using design software such as ABAQUS for practical engineering applications.

2 .

Conduct Structural and Geotechnical Modelling – Perform analysis and design of structures and geotechnical systems using industry-standard software tools, including geotechnical analysis using Rocscience and foundation design

3 .

Apply Hydrological / Water Resources Engineering Software – Use tools like HEC-RAS/ HEC-HMS to model hydraulic systems conduct river analysis/ hydrological modelling.

4 .

Implement Building Information Modeling (BIM) – Create and manage civil engineering projects using BIM software like Revit and Navisworks for architectural and structural modeling, as well as project collaboration.

5 .

Integrate Programming and Computational Tools – Apply MATLAB software to automate engineering calculations, analyze data, and solve real-world civil engineering problems.

Nam-Ho Kim, Bhavani V. Sankar, Introduction to Finite Element Analysis and Design, Wiley, 2nd Edition (2019)

2 .

2 .

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ER5601 : Numerical Weather Prediction { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1:
Basics of weather models Different spatial and temporal scales in NWP, Basic structure of numerical models and their applications, Governing equations, Map projections, Vertical coordinate system Global models, Regional models, Mesoscale models, Hydrostatic & non-hydrostatic assumption. [Duration: 6 hours]
Module 2:
Data assimilation Basic observational methods, Upper air observations, Surface synoptic observations, Weather Radars, Satellites and Synoptic charts, Analysis of surface and upper-air charts, Station models. Objective analysis schemes, data assimilation techniques, Initialization, Predictability and Ensemble forecasting. [Duration: 8 hours]
Module 3: Numerical Solutions Finite difference method-Forward and centered finite difference methods, Semi – implicit method and computational instability Computation of Jacobian and Laplacian Solution of Helmholtz and Poisson equations using relaxation method Spectral method, spherical harmonics [Duration: 6 hours]
Module 4: Atmospheric models Barotropic or Single level primitive model and instability Two level primitive equation model multilevel primitive equation models. Sigma coordinate system [Duration: 8 hours]
Module 5: Parameterization Parameterization of sub-grid scale physical processes: planetary boundary layer, moist microphysics physics, cumulus convection, radiation, air-sea interaction processes, and land surface processes. [Duration: 8 hours]

Course Objective

1 .

1. The course deals with the basic structure of weather models including initial conditions (data assimilation), fundamental equations that represents the dynamics and physical parameterizations, and numerical solutions. In detail, it educates model details such as map projections, vertical coordinate systems, etc types of observations, instrumentation and different objective analysis techniques to prepare initial conditions.
2 .

2. The application of finite difference methods to solve NWP models is introduced and detailed derivations to understand NWP model stability. The course delivers hierarchy of atmospheric models starting from single level model to multi-level models and sub-grid scale parameterization that indicates the sole nature of local phenomena.

Course Outcome

1 .

After the completion of the course, the students will be able
CO1 Structure of a numerical model and different components of numerical model
C02 Current status of atmospheric observations and concept of objective analysis and data assimilation
CO3 Provides detailed understanding of numerical solutions of atmospheric models and their stability
CO4 Familiarisation of hierarchy of atmospheric models starting from single level model to multi-level models
CO5 Different types of parameterization schemes that control numerical models performance

1 .

Holton J. R. and G. J. Hakim, An Introduction to Dynamical Meteorology, Academic Press (ELSEVIER) , Fifth Edition, 2013

2 .

Lynch A. H. and and J. J. Cassano, Applied Atmospheric Dynamics, John Wiley and Sons Ltd , 2005

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Haltiner G.J., Numerical Weather Prediction, John Wiley & Sons Inc , 1971

2 .

Haltiner G. J. and F.L.Martin, Dynamical and Physical Meteorology, McGraw-Hill Publcations , 1957

6518.t: FP4209: Separation Techniques in Food Processing
6518.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : FP4209 : Separation Techniques in Food Processing { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Introduction to Separation Techniques in Food Industry
-Overview of separation processes
-Definition and significance in food processing.
-Classification of separation processes
-Mechanical, thermal, diffusional, and other separation methods.
-Real-world examples highlighting the importance of separation techniques in product quality and safety.
Module 2: Various Separation Processes and Phase Equilibrium
-Gas-liquid separation
-Gas-solid separation
-Liquid-liquid separation
-Liquid-solid separation
-Understanding phase diagrams and their relevance to separation processes.
-Distillation
Module 3: Supercritical Fluid Extraction (SCFE)
-Introduction to SCF
-Definition and unique properties of supercritical fluids.
-Properties of SCF such as solvent power, diffusivity, and selectivity.
-Food applications of SCFE such as extraction of flavors, fragrances, and essential oils.
-Numerical problems in determining the parameters in SCF.
Module 4: Chemical Separation Techniques
-Coagulation and flocculation mechanisms and their roles in particle aggregation.
-Chromatographic separation
-Principle of adsorption
-Ion exchange methods
Module 5: Mechanical Separation Techniques
-Sedimentation: Principles and equipment used for settling particles.
-Centrifugation: Principles, types of centrifuges and their applications in separating components based on density differences, Safety and troubleshoot
-Filtration: Basics of filtration, types of filters, and common challenges encountered.
Module 6: Membrane Separation Technology
-Introduction to membrane processes: Microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, reverse osmosis, ion exchange, and electrodialysis.
-Physical characteristics of membranes: Material properties and membrane configurations.
-Factors affecting reverse osmosis process: Pressure, temperature, and concentration polarization.
-Operation layout of modules: Arrangement and integration of membrane units.
-Electrodialysis and pervaporation: Principles and applications in food processing.
-Application of membrane technology in food industry
Module 7: Powder Separation
-Classification of powders: Based on particle size and distribution.
-Separation of powders: Techniques such as sieving and air classification.
-Sieving: Equipment types and factors affecting efficiency.
-Air classification: Principles and factors influencing performance.
-Cyclone application: Design and use in particle separation.
-Air separation: Methods and equipment used.
-Particle size distribution: Measurement techniques and significance in food processing.

Course Objective

1 .

To comprehend fundamental separation processes in food processing
2 .

To analyze phase equilibria and their application in separation techniques
3 .

To evaluate advanced separation technologies and their food industry applications
4 .

To apply mechanical and chemical separation methods to enhance food quality and safety

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Define and describe various separation processes utilized in the food industry, including mechanical, thermal, diffusional, and other methods.
2. Explain the significance of phase diagrams in separation processes and their application in gas-liquid, gas-solid, liquid-liquid, and liquid-solid separations.
3. Demonstrate the use of supercritical fluid extraction (SCFE) in extracting flavors, fragrances, and essential oils from food products, including solving numerical problems related to SCF parameters.
4. Compare and contrast mechanical separation techniques such as sedimentation, centrifugation, and filtration, evaluating their principles, equipment, and applications in food processing.
5. Assess the effectiveness of membrane separation technologies, including microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, and reverse osmosis, in terms of factors like pressure, temperature, and concentration polarization, and their applications in the food industry.

Essential Reading

1 .

N. Anantharaman K. M. Meera Sheriffa Begum, Elements of Mass Transferring, PHI Learning

2 .

CM Narayanan and BC Bhattacharya, Mechanical Operations for Chemical Engineers, Khanna Publisher

Supplementary Reading

1 .

A. Rushton, A S Ward and R G Holdich, Solid-Liquid Filtration and separation Technology, Wiley-VCH

2 .

M A Mchugh and V J Krukonis, Super Critical Fluid Extraction-Principle and Practice, Butterworth-Heinemann

8054.t: PA5003: Review of Contemporary Global Architecture
8054.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PA5003 : Review of Contemporary Global Architecture { 1-0-3 / 3}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I
Introduction to architectural review and writing
Module II
Review of architectural works from Post industrial revolution: using examples from Neo-classical and Gothic Revival versus early iron and concrete construction
Module III
Review of architectural works from High Modern and Late Modern styles.
Module IV
Review of architectural works from Post-modern, Hi-tech and Neo-modern styles.
Module V
Understanding the recent trends in architecture across the globe: an overview of recent trends and practices followed by architects across the globe (focusing mainly on 21st century architecture).
Review of contemporary trends in architecture (Sustainable architecture, Biomimcry / Biophilia in architecture, Impact of digital design and computer aided visualization in architecture (example: parametric design, etc.).
Module VI
Review of recent architectural trends in South east Asian countries: review of works of selected architects (focusing mainly on 21st century architecture).

Course Objective

1 .

To develop verbal and written communicative skills for appraisal of architectural works, both national and international, with special focus on recent architectural trends across the globe

Course Outcome

1 .

• Developing abilities to understand and communicate architectural concepts and design ideas concisely, and effectively, in both verbal and textual formats.
• Understanding some of the contemporary trends in architecture based on the changing social, cultural, economic, political, environment conditions and advancement in technology.
• Developing the ability to appraise architectural works based on the social, cultural, political and economic context in which they were built.
Besides the review of architectural works from previously taught themes in the subjects focusing on evolution of architecture, this subject shall also focus on recent trends in architectural works across the globe.
• A recognition of the need for, and an ability to engage in, life-long learning
• An ability to apply knowledge of architecture
• An ability to communicate effectively
• An ability to function on multidisciplinary teams
• An understanding of professional and ethical responsibilities

Supplementary Reading
